name: voting-based-cooperation
context: Multi-agent systems where several agents produce candidate answers or evaluations on the same task and the system needs to return a single decision that reflects the group's collective judgment rather than any individual agent's output. Unlike debate, agents do not argue with each other — they vote, and a tallying mechanism produces the final outcome.
benefits: Aggregates diverse perspectives without requiring agents to justify their positions
Produces auditable decisions with a record of who voted for what
Handles genuine disagreement without requiring convergence dialogue
Scales to large electorates without combinatorial complexity
tradeoffs: Majority rule can entrench dominant agents regardless of expertise
Agents may vote strategically rather than truthfully
No mechanism for agents to revise beliefs based on others' evidence
All voting methods are subject to Arrow's impossibility theorem
use_cases: Medical triage: three specialist agents recommend tests; five generalist voters rank and tally
Code review: multiple agents flag different vulnerability classes; a coordinator tallies by severity
Content moderation: diverse perspective agents vote on appropriateness; threshold determines action
Research synthesis: multiple fact-checking agents vote on claim accuracy
avoid_when: Expertise is concentrated in one agent and others have no meaningful signal
Time pressure requires immediate single-agent response
The task requires negotiation or iterative refinement rather than independent judgment
anti_patterns: Returning a single agent's output as final without tallying
Giving all voters identical prompts (no diversity of perspective)
No mechanism to handle ties or low-confidence outcomes
No mechanism to detect or discourage strategic voting behavior
design_principles: Every voter must have a distinct perspective or expertise — identical agents add no value
The final decision must be the outcome of the tally, not a single agent's output
The ballot record must be persisted for post-hoc audit
best_practices: Use weighted voting where voter expertise is known (role-based weights)
Define explicit tie-breaking rules before deployment
Log the full ballot (who voted what) alongside the outcome for accountability
Use Borda Count for multi-candidate elections where preference order matters
Preserve minority votes and dissenting opinions in audit trail for high-stakes decisions
references: Wang et al., Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models, 2022 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171
Lin et al., LLM-Blender: Ensembling Large Language Models with pairwise comparison and preferential reasoning, ACL 2024 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02561
